A floating, resizable browser that sits on top of your games, launcher, or any app.
✗ Display over other apps: not allowed yet (required). Tap the button below, find Overlay Browser in the list, and turn it on.
✗ Notifications: off. Turn them on to get Show/Close controls in the notification shade.
How see-through the floating window is, from 10% (barely there) to 100% (solid). Also under ⋮ → Opacity on the window. If you set it too faint to find, turn it back up here.
Brave found (%1$s). The menu can send any page to Brave.
Brave isn\'t installed. The floating browser still works; it just can\'t hand pages off to Brave.
Open Brave in a floating window
Freeform windows: on. Brave can open as a floating window.
Freeform windows: off. Brave will open full screen. To make it float, go to Developer options → \"Enable freeform windows\", then restart.
Freeform windows: couldn\'t detect. If Brave opens full screen, go to Developer options → \"Enable freeform windows\", then restart.

• Drag the ⠿ grip or the empty part of the toolbar to move the window. Drag a bottom corner to resize it.
• 🔒 locks the position and size. — minimizes to a bubble: tap the bubble to restore it, long-press it for more options. Audio keeps playing while minimized.
• Touching the page doesn't take your gamepad away from the game. The window only takes keyboard focus while you type. Tap outside it, or press Back, to give control back to the game.
• Watching a video? Tap the ▣ button on the bar: the window shows only the player and takes the video's exact shape, and keeps that shape as you resize it. YouTube videos do this on their own (turn it off in ⋮). Tap ▣ again for the full page.
• ⋮ → Opacity makes the window see-through (10–100%), handy for keeping an eye on the game behind a guide or video.
• Add the "Float browser" tile in Quick Settings to show/hide the window from anywhere.
• Share any link to "Open in floating browser" to open it in the floating window.
